clues: Otis rowed either the Minnow or the Skipjack.
Amara and Felix rowed the Skipjack and the Teacup, in some order.
Neither the varnished nor the ash oars went out on the Skipjack.
Whoever had the blue-tipped oars rowed either the Pebble or the Teacup.
Neither Felix nor Otis used the varnished oars.
One of Felix and Amara used the varnished oars, and the other used the spruce oars.
hints: Look at the Skipjack in the box where oars meet dinghies. Which oars could have gone out on it?
Clue 3 crosses off two kinds of oars for the Skipjack, and clue 4 keeps the blue-tipped oars away from it. Put them together.
So the Skipjack's rower used the spruce oars. Clues 5 and 6 give Felix the spruce oars, so Felix rowed the Skipjack.

solution.key_idea: Clues 3 and 4 leave the Skipjack only the spruce oars, and clues 5 and 6 make those Felix's.
steps: Clue 3 rules out the varnished and ash oars for the Skipjack, and clue 4 the blue-tipped, so the Skipjack's rower used the spruce oars.
Clue 2 keeps Otis and Walt off the Skipjack and Teacup, so by clue 1 Otis rowed the Minnow, and Walt the Pebble.
The Minnow's oars were not blue-tipped (clue 4), varnished (clue 5) or spruce (the Skipjack's), so Otis used the ash oars.
By clues 5 and 6, Felix used the spruce oars and Amara the varnished, so Felix rowed the Skipjack.
By clue 2, Amara rowed the Teacup, and Walt used the blue-tipped oars on the Pebble.
solution.epilogue: Felix rowed the Skipjack with spruce, Otis the Minnow with ash, Walt the Pebble with blue-tipped oars, and Amara the Teacup with varnished. Who moved Felix's own dinghy stayed a puzzle.

tip: When two people share two dinghies in some order, cross everyone else off those dinghies at once.
